class.name: NNBTParallel
class.brief_description: Ticks all its enabled child nodes and combines their accumulated results using [member success_policy] and [member failure_policy]. The policy is evaluated after every child tick and the node early-exits as soon as the outcome is decided.
class.description:
A parallel node runs its enabled children concurrently. Within one run it remembers every child's terminal result and does not tick that child again until the next run. A child that returned [code]RUNNING[/code] has no remembered result yet and is ticked again on the next tick. Disabled children are not ticked and are excluded from every count.
[code]SKIP[/code] results count as [code]SUCCESS[/code] for the policy evaluation. [code]SKIP[/code] never caused a failure and a lone [code]SKIP[/code] child returned [code]SUCCESS[/code], so the default policies reproduce the historical behaviour exactly.
The policies are evaluated after every child tick against the results accumulated so far in the current run: [codeblock] success_met = success_policy == REQUIRE_ALL ? num_success == num_enabled : num_success > 0 failure_met = failure_policy == REQUIRE_ALL ? num_failure == num_enabled : num_failure > 0 if success_met and failure_met: result = FAILURE elif success_met: result = SUCCESS elif failure_met: result = FAILURE elif num_success + num_failure == num_enabled: result = FAILURE else: result = RUNNING [/codeblock] [code]num_enabled[/code] is the number of enabled children and [code]num_success[/code] and [code]num_failure[/code] only count children with a terminal result, so children that are still running do not yet satisfy a "require all" policy. The precedence is therefore the both-met [code]FAILURE[/code] tie (which matches the historical failure-before-success behaviour), then [code]SUCCESS[/code], then [code]FAILURE[/code], then [code]RUNNING[/code] while some children have no terminal result yet. The final [code]FAILURE[/code] is the documented fallback for mixed outcomes under [constant SUCCESS_REQUIRE_ALL] and [constant FAILURE_REQUIRE_ALL], where every child is terminal but neither policy is satisfied.
As soon as the result is [code]SUCCESS[/code] or [code]FAILURE[/code] the node returns it immediately and interrupts the children that are still running. Children that have already finished are not interrupted again. The per-run memory is cleared when a new run starts, on reset, and on interrupt. A child added during a run participates from the next tick, and a removed child is no longer considered.
The defaults ([constant SUCCESS_REQUIRE_ALL] and [constant FAILURE_REQUIRE_ONE]) fail immediately when any child fails and otherwise return [code]SUCCESS[/code] only once every enabled child has succeeded. Until then they return [code]RUNNING[/code].
An empty parallel, or one whose children are all disabled, has no enabled children. "Require all" is then trivially true and "require one" is false, so the node returns [code]SUCCESS[/code] only with [constant SUCCESS_REQUIRE_ALL] and [constant FAILURE_REQUIRE_ONE]; every other policy combination returns [code]FAILURE[/code].

members.member: How many enabled children must return [code]FAILURE[/code] for the parallel node to fail. [constant FAILURE_REQUIRE_ONE] (default) fails when at least one enabled child fails; [constant FAILURE_REQUIRE_ALL] fails only when every enabled child fails. Values outside the [enum FailurePolicy] range are rejected with a single engine error that names [code]set_failure_policy[/code], the received value and the valid range; the previous policy is kept.

How many enabled children must return [code]SUCCESS[/code] (or [code]SKIP[/code], which counts as a success) for the parallel node to succeed. [constant SUCCESS_REQUIRE_ALL] (default) requires every enabled child to succeed; [constant SUCCESS_REQUIRE_ONE] requires at least one. Values outside the [enum SuccessPolicy] range are rejected with a single engine error that names [code]set_success_policy[/code], the received value and the valid range; the previous policy is kept.

constants.constant: The parallel node returns [code]SUCCESS[/code] only when every enabled child succeeded. This is the default.
The parallel node returns [code]SUCCESS[/code] when at least one enabled child succeeded.
The parallel node returns [code]FAILURE[/code] when at least one enabled child failed. This is the default.
The parallel node returns [code]FAILURE[/code] only when every enabled child failed.
